findings.title: used_cnt published before the write barrier
findings.explanation: The used-ring entries and the packet data copied into the peer's buffers must be visible to the peer before it sees the new used_cnt. Here used_cnt is written first and rte_wmb() comes after it. With write-combining mapping, which this patch enables, the stores can arrive out of order. The peer may then read stale used entries or stale packet data.

findings.title: avail_cnt published before the write barrier
findings.explanation: The new descriptors are copied into the remote desc ring, and avail_cnt is written before rte_wmb(). The peer can see the new avail_cnt before the descriptor writes arrive, especially with write-combining, and then use stale buffer addresses.

findings.title: Failure mid multi-seg packet leaves partial segments published
findings.explanation: A goto end_of_tx at segment i>0 (ring full, zero-length descriptor, or ioremap failure) leaves the earlier segments in tx_used, written without the EOP flag. txq->last_used has already moved past them and sw_ring holds the mbufs. But nb_tx is not incremented and nb_tx_free is not decremented. used_cnt is then published, so the peer sees a packet with no end and merges it with the next one. The caller still owns the mbuf because it was reported as not sent, yet a later cleanup frees those segments: use-after-free or double free. If nb_tx==0, last_used has advanced but nothing is flushed, so the ring state goes out of sync.
findings.suggestion: Before starting a packet, check that all nb_segs descriptors are available and valid. On a failure partway through, roll txq->last_used and nb_mbufs back to their values at the start of the packet.

findings.title: Packet loop bounded by descriptor count can read unpublished entries
findings.explanation: used_nb counts descriptors (segments), but the outer loop runs once per packet, and the inner loop takes as many descriptors as each packet needs. For multi-segment packets, count packets can need more than used_nb descriptors. The loop then reads used-ring entries the peer has not published yet: stale lengths and flags, and mbufs that hold no data.
findings.suggestion: Track the number of descriptors consumed and stop when it reaches used_nb, including inside the inner while loop.

findings.title: mbuf alloc failure mid-packet corrupts ring state
findings.explanation: When the new-mbuf allocation fails, last_used has already been advanced but the slot is not refilled and last_avail does not move. The current packet is not counted, even though buffers[nb_rx] was already set. The received mbuf stays in sw_ring and is later overwritten (a leak). On the next call, dequeue resumes partway through the packet and treats continuation segments as new packets.
findings.suggestion: Allocate the replacement mbuf before consuming the descriptor, or roll last_used back on failure, so ring state only changes at packet boundaries.

findings.title: Peer address bounds check is off-by-one and ignores copy length
findings.explanation: The check uses `<=` instead of `<`, so an address exactly one past the end of the window counts as valid. The function also only checks the start address. Enqueue then copies up to tx_item->len bytes there, and both the address and the length come from the peer's descriptor. An address near the window's end makes the copy run past the mapped BAR region.
findings.suggestion: Use `addr < base + mw_size` and pass the length so the function can check `addr + len <= base + mw_size`. Return NULL otherwise.

findings.title: Peer-supplied length not validated against mbuf buffer size
findings.explanation: data_len is taken directly from the used ring, which the peer writes, and is never compared with buf_len - headroom. A bad or corrupt value gives an mbuf whose data_len is larger than its buffer, so the application reads out of bounds.
findings.suggestion: Clamp or reject when rx_item->len > rxm_t->buf_len - RTE_PKTMBUF_HEADROOM.

findings.title: Truncating data_len leaves pkt_len inconsistent
findings.explanation: The function shrinks the caller's mbuf data_len to fit the remote buffer but leaves pkt_len unchanged. The mbuf's lengths no longer agree, and the data is silently cut off.
findings.suggestion: Reject the oversized segment, or copy only min(data_len, len) without modifying the caller's mbuf.
